title: Drishyam 3 Hits Prime Video on June 18. Georgekutty's Most Dangerous Game Yet Comes to 200 Countries at Once.
excerpt: The biggest Malayalam blockbuster of the year — ₹236 crore and counting — lands on streaming exactly four weeks after theatres, in Malayalam plus Tamil, Telugu and Kannada. The diaspora has been waiting.
body:
There is a particular kind of silence that falls over a Mohanlal film when Georgekutty stops talking and just *looks* at someone. It is the silence of a man calculating three moves ahead while everyone else is still on move one. For thirteen years, across three films and a dozen remakes, that look has been the most reliable thrill in Indian cinema. And on **June 18**, it arrives in your living room.

<youtube></youtube>

**Drishyam 3**, the year's biggest Malayalam blockbuster, begins streaming on **Amazon Prime Video** worldwide — in Malayalam, with dubbed versions in **Tamil, Telugu and Kannada**, across more than 200 countries and territories. That last detail is the one that matters for the diaspora. No more grainy theatre leaks, no more waiting for a friend in Kochi to explain the ending over a crackly call. This time, an NRI in New Jersey and a fan in Kottayam press play on the same Friday.



> **"Beyond the mystery, it is rooted in a deeply human story about family, love, and survival." — **Mohanlal**

The numbers explain the appetite."**


> "Georgekutty is a character who has stayed with audiences for many years, and that love is something deeply cherished. Beyond the mystery, it is rooted in a deeply human story about family, love, and survival." — **Mohanlal**

The numbers explain the appetite. Directed once again by **Jeethu Joseph**, Drishyam 3 crossed ₹200 crore in just ten days and has sailed past **₹236 crore worldwide**, making it the highest-grossing chapter in the franchise and one of the biggest Malayalam films ever made. For a series that began in 2013 as a modest thriller about a cable TV operator outwitting the police, that is a staggering arc — proof that intelligence, patiently written, still outsells spectacle.

And the timing is its own statement. Four weeks from theatre to stream is aggressive, a calculated bet that the buzz hasn't cooled and that the global Malayali audience — the engine of Mollywood's box office — is ready to push the digital numbers higher. Prime Video announced the date with a poster of Georgekutty flanked by Rani, Anju and Anu, captioned simply: *"Georgekutty and family awaits you."* Loaded words, for anyone who knows what this family has survived.

What are they surviving this time? Without spoiling the famously twisty plot: years have passed since Drishyam 2, and Georgekutty has done the unthinkable — turned his own buried past into a hit film. Then two journalists start digging into the real story behind the story. A marriage proposal for daughter Anju curdles into a trap. Old adversaries return with sharpened motives. And the protector must once again think his way out of a corner closing in from every side. **Meena** returns as Rani, with **Ansiba Hassan**, **Esther Anil**, **Siddique**, **Murali Gopy** and **Asha Sharath** rounding out a cast that has aged into these roles like family.

Critics were not unanimously dazzled. Cinema Express noted the film "lacks sorely" the jaw-dropping *how-did-he-cover-that* moments that defined the earlier instalments — though it praised Jeethu Joseph for "bravely opting for a profound ending." That is a fair warning and also, frankly, a high-class problem: when your franchise has trained audiences to expect genius twists every fifteen minutes, merely *very good* feels like a letdown. The box office suggests audiences forgave it instantly.

For the diaspora, the franchise has always carried something extra. Drishyam 2 premiered straight to Prime Video in 2021, mid-pandemic, and became a word-of-mouth phenomenon precisely because it reached living rooms in Toronto and London and Dubai at the same moment it reached Thrissur. It made the Georgekutty saga a shared global text — the kind of film an uncle in Houston and a cousin in Kerala could argue about on the same WhatsApp thread. Drishyam 3 inherits that reach on day one.

A word on the Malayalam wave it rides: this has been a monster year for Mollywood, with **L2: Empuraan** and **Thudarum** also crossing the ₹200-crore mark. Malayalam cinema, long the connoisseur's choice, is now posting the kind of numbers that make Bollywood nervous — and doing it with writing, not budgets.

So clear your Thursday night. Georgekutty is back, the family is in danger again, and for once you don't need a plane ticket to find out how he gets them out. Just Prime Video, June 18, in the language of your choice.
